# SSH cluster operations

## Topology and trust model

The managed cluster is a three-node full mesh on the private LAN:

| Node | Current cluster address | Accepted clusterops SSH sources |
|---|---|---|
| node1 | 10.100.203.10 | node2 (10.100.203.11), node3 (10.100.203.12) |
| node2 | 10.100.203.11 | node1 (10.100.203.10), node3 (10.100.203.12) |
| node3 | 10.100.203.12 | node1 (10.100.203.10), node2 (10.100.203.11) |

Each node has the non-root account \`clusterops\`. Each node generated its own Ed25519 identity at \`/home/clusterops/.ssh/id_ed25519\`; private keys stay on their source node. Each destination has exactly the other two public keys in \`authorized_keys\`, with an OpenSSH \`from="peer-IP"\` restriction on each entry. The clusterops password is locked, and the SSH daemon disables password and keyboard-interactive authentication.

The stable names node1, node2, and node3 are maintained in \`/etc/hosts\`. The clusterops SSH client profile uses the per-node identity, strict known-host checking, the managed \`known_hosts\` file, and \`BatchMode yes\`. SSH is socket-activated: \`ssh.socket\` is enabled and should be active; \`ssh.service\` may be inactive until the first connection.

## Verify all six connections

Run the checks directly on each source node. Do not use one node as a control plane for another. The commands below must return exit status 0 and print the destination hostname.

~~~sh
# On node1
sudo -u clusterops -H -- ssh -4 -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=8 node2 hostname
sudo -u clusterops -H -- ssh -4 -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=8 node3 hostname

# On node2
sudo -u clusterops -H -- ssh -4 -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=8 node1 hostname
sudo -u clusterops -H -- ssh -4 -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=8 node3 hostname

# On node3
sudo -u clusterops -H -- ssh -4 -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=8 node1 hostname
sudo -u clusterops -H -- ssh -4 -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=8 node2 hostname
~~~

On every node, verify names, key file permissions, peer-only authorization, and the socket-activated server:

~~~sh
getent hosts node1 node2 node3
stat -c '%A %U:%G %n' /home/clusterops/.ssh /home/clusterops/.ssh/id_ed25519 /home/clusterops/.ssh/authorized_keys
awk 'NF { print $1 }' /home/clusterops/.ssh/authorized_keys
ssh-keygen -F node1 -f /home/clusterops/.ssh/known_hosts
ssh-keygen -F node2 -f /home/clusterops/.ssh/known_hosts
ssh-keygen -F node3 -f /home/clusterops/.ssh/known_hosts
sshd -t
systemctl is-enabled ssh.socket
systemctl is-active ssh.socket
~~~

The authorization check should show two \`from="..."\` clauses, one for each peer, and no self entry. Do not print the complete authorized_keys file in tickets or reports.

## Confirm persistence across reboot

Reboot only one node at a time, after the six-path check passes and the remaining nodes are healthy. Use the managed maintenance or console procedure for the reboot; do not reboot all three nodes together.

After the node returns, run these checks directly on it:

~~~sh
hostname
getent hosts node1 node2 node3
test -x /usr/sbin/sshd
test -r /home/clusterops/.ssh/id_ed25519
test -r /home/clusterops/.ssh/authorized_keys
test -r /home/clusterops/.ssh/known_hosts
sshd -t
systemctl is-enabled ssh.socket
systemctl is-active ssh.socket
~~~

Then rerun both outbound paths from the rebooted node and the two inbound paths to it from the other nodes. Repeat for each node, one at a time. A socket-activated service can leave \`ssh.service\` inactive until a connection arrives; \`ssh.socket\` being enabled and active is the persistence check. The service unit creates \`/run/sshd\` when it starts, so check that runtime directory after the first post-reboot connection if needed.

## Recover an interrupted SSH service

Use the node's direct management console or direct InfraSet execution when SSH itself is unavailable. Collect evidence first:

~~~sh
systemctl status ssh.socket ssh.service --no-pager -n 40
journalctl -u ssh.socket -u ssh.service -n 60 --no-pager
sshd -t
~~~

For a missing runtime directory or missing host keys, repair only the SSH runtime prerequisites:

~~~sh
install -d -o root -g root -m 755 /run/sshd
ssh-keygen -A
sshd -t
~~~

\`ssh-keygen -A\` only creates missing server host keys. Do not replace existing host keys unless the operator has deliberately approved a host-identity rotation, because that requires refreshing \`known_hosts\` on all three nodes.

After \`sshd -t\` succeeds, restore the enabled socket and clear stale failure state:

~~~sh
systemctl reset-failed ssh.service ssh.socket
systemctl enable ssh.socket
systemctl restart ssh.socket
if systemctl is-active --quiet ssh.service; then
    systemctl reload ssh.service
fi
systemctl is-active ssh.socket
~~~

Finally rerun the six-path matrix. If \`sshd -t\` identifies a configuration error, correct that directive and validate again before restarting the socket. Keep the per-node private identity in place; if a user key is lost, generate a replacement on its source node and install only its new public key on the two peer destinations, then rerun the matrix.

echo '=== accounts ==='
getent passwd clusterops
awk -F: '$3 >= 1000 && $1 != "nobody" {print $1 ":" $3 ":" $6}' /etc/passwd
echo '=== ssh packages ==='
dpkg-query -W -f='\${Package} \${Version}\n' 'openssh*' 2>/dev/null || true
echo '=== ssh file inventory ==='
sudo -n find /home/clusterops/.ssh /root/.ssh /etc/ssh -maxdepth 2 -type f -printf '%m %u:%g %p\n' 2>/dev/null | sort
echo '=== authorized key metadata ==='
sudo -n -u clusterops -H awk 'NF { for (i=1;i<=NF;i++) if ($i ~ /^(ssh-|ecdsa-|sk-)/) { print "line=" NR " keytype=" $i " option_prefix=" substr($0,1,index($0,$i)-1); n++; break } } END { print "key_entries=" n+0 }' /home/clusterops/.ssh/authorized_keys 2>/dev/null || true
echo '=== client effective settings ==='
for h in node1 node2 node3; do
  echo "--- $h ---"
  sudo -n -u clusterops -H ssh -G "$h" 2>/dev/null | awk '$1 ~ /^(user|hostname|batchmode|stricthostkeychecking|userknownhostsfile|identityfile)$/ {print}'
done
echo '=== server effective settings ==='
sudo -n /usr/sbin/sshd -T 2>/dev/null | awk '$1 ~ /^(pubkeyauthentication|passwordauthentication|kbdinteractiveauthentication|permitrootlogin|authorizedkeysfile|allowusers|allowgroups|listenaddress|port)$/ {print}'
echo '=== name mappings ==='
getent ahostsv4 node1 node2 node3 | awk '{print $1, $5}' | sort -u
awk '$1 !~ /^#/ && NF >= 2 { for (i=2;i<=NF;i++) if ($i == "node1" || $i == "node2" || $i == "node3") print $i " " $1 }' /etc/hosts | sort
echo '=== firewall ==='
if command -v ufw >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo -n ufw status verbose; else echo 'ufw: unavailable'; fi
if command -v nft >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo -n nft -nn list ruleset; else echo 'nft: unavailable'; fi
if command -v iptables-save >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo -n iptables-save; else echo 'iptables-save: unavailable'; fi
echo '=== listeners ==='
sudo -n ss -lntup 2>&1
echo '=== running services ==='
systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running --no-legend 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}'
echo '=== candidate artifacts ==='
for d in /tmp /var/tmp /home/clusterops/.ssh /etc/ssh; do
  if [ -d "$d" ]; then
    sudo -n find "$d" -maxdepth 2 -type f \( -iname '*ssh*' -o -iname '*.bak' -o -iname '*.backup' -o -iname '*.tmp' -o -iname '*debug*' -o -iname '*key*' -o -iname 'authorized_keys*' -o -iname 'known_hosts*' \) -printf '%p %u:%g %m\n' 2>/dev/null
  fi
done | sort
